title: You guys were pretty brutal about my ARPG combat last time. I reworked a lot of it - better direction?
author: freesoulapps
selftext:
This is **The Lost Colony**, an isometric sci-fi ARPG I’m building in Unreal Engine. I’ve been developing most of it with AI coding agents, mainly GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5, and using Meshy for some of the 3D/animation work.

I posted the combat here a few days ago and got a lot of useful criticism. The main things people called out were the stiff movement/animations, weak hit reactions, attacks lacking anticipation and weight, enemies feeling like they were just wandering around, and some grounding/readability problems.

I’ve been working through that feedback and changed quite a lot since then, player/enemy animations, hit reactions, combat feedback, HUD/readability, enemy behavior and some of the overall pacing.

It’s **still not finished**, and I know there’s more work to do.

I’m mostly trying to understand whether this is now moving in the right direction.

What still stands out as weak or wrong?

And if you could pick the **2–3 things that would make the biggest difference next**, what would you focus on?

comments.author: KS-Wolf-1978
comments.body: Looks good, the only bad thing is jumpy non-smooth scrolling, but should be easily fixable.

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body: Thanks. I see the camera/scrolling issue too now. I’ll add smoothing to the next pass, glad the rest is moving in the right direction.

comments.author: Fuzzzy420
comments.body:
Working on a very similar game. 
Some feedback: 
Player animations don't feel good. 
Hit feedback
The gun feels like a pee shooter 
You don't get any damage?

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body:
Thanks, this is useful. Player animation and weapon impact are still two of the main things I’m working on.

When you say the gun feels like a pea shooter, is it mainly the recoil/audio, enemy hit reaction, VFX, or all of it? I’ll also check the player-damage feedback because it clearly isn’t reading well in this clip.

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body:
I can't really hear or see getting hit. It's a lot of laser pewpew sounds. Vfx for the player gun could get a bit more love. Don't like the dash at all   
Damage feels very low for robots and player

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body: Got it, that helps a lot. Sounds like I need a proper weapon-feel pass: stronger player damage feedback, better gun VFX/audio, more impact on enemies, and another look at the dash and overall damage/TTK. Thanks.

comments.author: Classroom-Obvious
comments.body: still looks like shit, and will not be paying for this. Thank you for posting on a a alt so I remember what not to do with my game

comments.author: SproutsJeremy
comments.body:
It’s like 15 FPS lol, choppy and unplayable. If it was 60 FPS, I’m ngl it would look pretty impressive and appealing. Right now it doesn’t look good.

Imo you need to drop everything you are doing and work on optimization. Then you have a genuinely good and very strong showcase. 

Anyways, hope development goes well, and keep at it. Imo this looks like it has great potential

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body: Thanks. The source is actually 30 fps, so Reddit may be making the playback look worse, but you're the second person to call out the choppy scrolling. So there's clearly a smoothness issue there regardless. I'll look at the camera smoothing/frame pacing specifically.

replies.author: SproutsJeremy
replies.body: Aw yeah reddit can be bad for posting previews for sure. Do you have a better preview on youtube or similar that’s at the original 30 fps? Would love to check out a smoother video

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body:
Yes, here 16:9 video:
https://youtu.be/o9eBQACEaCQ?si=YepiqUHBKccCglYO

comments.author: darkoblivion000
comments.body:
Looking much better. I like the rolling animation. The pivoting at the waist of the mech is also pretty cool.

I think the scrolling as someone mentioned and also the lasers could use some polish. I know the red lines are supposed to be laser sight but something about them looks very low quality and out of place

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body:
Thanks. Good to hear the rolling and mech movement are reading better.

The scrolling is definitely going back on the list, and I agree on the red laser sights, they’re functional as telegraphs right now, but visually they look too simple compared with the rest of the scene. I’ll give those a proper VFX/material pass.

comments.author: Mobile-Bedroom9175
comments.body: Terrain and envrioment seems good . The things i liked most in POE2 was feeling of hit . You need to work on it . Player need to feel impact of hit or skill . And also character animatioins seems a bit off .A specially side step

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body:
Thanks, that’s useful. POE2 is a good reference for impact even though I’m aiming closer to The Ascent overall. Hit feel is clearly still one of the biggest gaps.

I’m also reworking the player locomotion/animation set, especially the sidestep, several people have called that one out now.

replies.author: Mobile-Bedroom9175
replies.body: Consider it also referance . Player see and feel elemental impact by shattering  or exploding monsters you know . Little visuals or implements makes big difference .

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body:
Yeah, that makes sense. I’m not aiming for POE2’s combat style overall, but its hit/death feedback is a really good reference.

I need damage to visibly change what’s happening, stronger reactions, stagger, sparks/debris, breakups or explosions where appropriate, instead of enemies just losing HP while looking mostly the same.
